Definition: from G303 and G5594; properly, to cool off, i.e. (figuratively) relieve:--refresh.
BiblicalUsage: The word appears once: 'The Lord give mercy unto the house of Onesiphorus; for he oft refreshed me, and was not ashamed of my chain.' It is cooling off, catching your breath — the refreshment of a friend who keeps coming to a prisoner in chains, when others have walked away.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for refreshing carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is Onesiphorus — the friend who kept coming, and was not ashamed of the chain.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
